summary: A front and rear range pair on the St. Lawrence ship channel at Verchères, established 1 May 1902; the nearby windmill became a signal station in 1909.

structures.note: Front tower rebuilt in 1929 (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett). LighthouseFriends says an enclosed lantern room; Rowlett describes a square wooden lantern. The 1902 front was a square wooden tower on a cribwork pier, 31 ft from pier to ventilator.
65 ft to the ventilator (1902 report). Rowlett calls the earlier rear light a 20 m (66 ft) square pyramidal skeletal tower; replaced in 2021 or 2022.

access.note: Front light: grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends). Rear light: site and tower closed, private property (Lighthouse Directory).

events.note: Front and rear range lights established 1 May 1902. Front: fixed white catoptric, 44 ft above summer river level, visible 12 miles. Rear: fixed white catoptric, 85 ft above summer river level, visible 15 miles.
Old stone windmill acquired by the Department, possession 1 April 1909; used as a marine signal station
Front tower rebuilt as a skeletal tower with an enclosed lantern room
Windmill signal station ended (LighthouseFriends gives 1949; Lighthouse Directory says about 1940; disputed)
Rear light replaced; Lighthouse Directory dates the present rear light to 2021 or 2022

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1910 Department report reprints the parish priest's notes, which give 1690; Rowlett gives 'around 1700'. The story gives the priest's date as the priest's and Rowlett's as Rowlett's.
LighthouseFriends says the signal station served until 1949; Rowlett says from 1909 to around 1940. The story gives both.
LighthouseFriends describes an enclosed lantern room; Rowlett describes a square wooden lantern on the 6 m skeletal tower. The story states both.

notes_for_editor: The 1902 Marine report (scan pp. 81-82) is the primary source for the 1 May 1902 range lights and their descriptions; the village paragraph is the second 'Two range lights were established on May 1, 1902' block on scan 81. Keeper rows: the 1902 list's 'Vercheres Village (Back) April 12, 1902' (scan 237, printed 60) carries no name on its OCR line; the link to Bousquet is by position, and the 1904 list (scan 167, printed 154) names him at the station on one OCR line. Checked in the archive.org viewer for the 1902 list (scan 237): the Village (front) row reads April 21, 1902; the Village (Back) row's date could not be read at legible resolution, so the 12 April 1902 reading rests on OCR. The 1904 list's date for Bousquet (23 June 1903) is OCR column-matched and not used. Guyon's April 1902 date in the 1904 list is also read by position; the story gives no date for Guyon. Ed. Chagnon and A. St. Pierre come only from the LighthouseFriends keeper table and were not found in the Department lists read. The windmill's 1690 date and the 1692 defence are the parish priest's notes, reprinted in the Department's 1910 report; the story attributes them to the priest. LighthouseFriends' text about the mast and telephone line is not checked against the Department's text. Felix Bousquet's $70 salary is LighthouseFriends' figure; the 1904 OCR may show $75 beside his row, not checked. The record's current heights (front 6.0 m, rear 24.5 m) are the current towers in Rowlett (front 6 m skeletal, 1929; rear 24.5 m skeletal, 2021 or 2022); they are not the 1902 figures. The current characteristic of each range light is F G (fixed green) in the Canadian Coast Guard list (entries 2319 and 2320) and continuous green in Rowlett. No storms, wrecks or rescues were found for this station.
